Breakfast.

Travel from Cusco to Puno on a Turismo Avalos tourist coach, stopping at major historic sites and scenic spots in the Andes. Along the way, you’ll see mountain landscapes and learn about Peru’s ancient civilisations.

Stops along the way:

1. Andahuaylillas. Visit the Church of San Pedro Apóstol, often called the “Sistine Chapel of South America”. Its elaborate paintings, carved altars and decorative details are a fine example of colonial religious art.

2. Raqchi. Explore an Inca archaeological site with the remains of a large temple dedicated to Viracocha, along with dwellings and storehouses that reveal how the empire was administered and supplied.

3. Sicuani. Stop for lunch.

4. La Raya. At approximately 4,300–4,400 metres above sea level, this is the highest point on the route. Look out over mountain peaks and broad Andean plateaus, or browse the small roadside market for local crafts.

5. Pukara. Learn about the pre-Inca culture of the same name and its place in Andean history.

Arrive in Puno at around 18:00. Transfer to the 4-star Casona Plaza hotel or a similar hotel of the same category and check in.

Optional: travel on the luxury Titicaca Train

Supplement: USD 295 per person. Trains depart on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, according to the operator’s timetable.

Take the Titicaca Train from Cusco to Puno on one of the world’s highest railway lines. The route crosses the Andes, with changing views of open plateaus and valleys along the way.

The train has a dining car, a bar car and a panoramic observation car. It stops near La Raya at over 4,300 metres above sea level, with views of mountain peaks and wide plains.

The fare includes a three-course lunch with a starter, main course and dessert.

Arrive in Puno at about 19:00, then transfer to your hotel and check in.
